followUps: What exactly does each of the four positions say?
If humans evolved, how do I read the verses saying Adam was made from clay?
Do I have to believe Adam had no parents to be a Muslim?
doubter.why: It is useful to learn that “The real dispute is narrow”, but the four positions are only named, never explained, and the clay verses in the question are not discussed.

followUps: What do 'human exceptionalism' and 'Adamic exceptionalism' mean?
What do most Muslims and Muslim institutions actually believe about evolution?
outsider.why: The main ideas (occasionalism, hermeneutics, the exceptionalism positions) are not explained, and “Institutional positions remain cautious” does not say which institutions or what they say.

followUps: What is al-Ghazali's rule for when a verse may be read non-literally, and how does Malik apply it?
What do the other Adam verses (clay, dust, sounding clay) say, and how does each position read them?
Which institutions are 'cautious' (Diyanet?), and what have they said?
student.why: Malik and Jalajel are good names, but only one verse (3:59) is given, al-Ghazali's hermeneutic is not explained, and no classical or institutional positions are set out.

followUps: What is the evidence for common descent (fossils, genomics, shared pseudogenes)?
What do population genetics say about minimum ancestral population size, and does a genealogical Adam fit?
When would Adam have lived on the Adamic-exceptionalism view?
scientist.why: The scientific perspective is one line (“Common descent is [Established].”), and the population-genetics objection is mentioned without any numbers.

followUps: My biology class made me feel I must choose between science and faith. Do I?
What do I say to family members who think accepting evolution is unbelief?
Is it safe for my faith to hold Adamic exceptionalism?
hurting.why: “Learning that these options exist often brings relief” is kind and true, but the page is too short to give that relief itself.

followUps: Why is the 'no exceptions' view judged scripturally incompatible, and by what standard?
How does Adamic exceptionalism handle humans who were not descended from Adam? Isn't that ad hoc?
How does guided creation fit with random mutation and natural selection, beyond saying 'unguided is metaphysics'?
skeptic.why: Critics are dismissed in three words (“Critics call this ad hoc”), and the page never explains why the fourth position fails or how humans not descended from Adam fit.

missing: A plain explanation of each of Malik's four positions and how each reads the Adam verses
The other Quran verses on Adam's creation, not only 3:59
Real science: the evidence for common descent and the population-genetics numbers
Al-Ghazali's interpretive rule explained, and how Malik applies it
Which institutions are cautious and what they have said
A fair account of critiques of Adamic exceptionalism and why 'no exceptions' is judged incompatible
strengths: Names a serious, current academic source (Malik, Routledge 2021) and Jalajel
Narrows the dispute honestly to whether Adam had ancestors
Clear separation of 'unguided' metaphysics from biology
Admits the population-genetics objection and its 'ad hoc' critique
Caution against reading Darwin into Ibn Khaldun
